title: Admin
subtitle: Server & content administration
images_subtitle: The platform image whitelist. Only enabled images can back a new server. You can add external images or delete unwanted images from the whitelist.
delete_image_title: Remove this image from the whitelist?
delete_image_desc: New servers can no longer be created from
cancel_build_desc: The build stops now and pushes nothing:
builds_subtitle: History of image build jobs and trigger controls. The build pod runs inside an isolated namespace with automated Trivy scans.
dockerfile_audit_hint: Archived on the build row for audit. Kaniko executes the `Dockerfile` inside the context tarball — this text is never executed.
download_context_hint: Downloads the uploaded context (.tar.gz) — it contains the Dockerfile that will actually be executed.
context_sha256_hint: Approval pins this digest. Builds reject subsequent uploads that do not match it. Use sha256sum to verify downloaded files during offline review.
context_sha256_missing: No build context is available, or it predates digest recording. The submitter must upload it again.
context_sha256_downloaded: The digest matches the downloaded file. Approval pins this content.
context_sha256_stale: The downloaded version ({{digest}}…) was replaced by a new upload. Download and review the latest version.
approve_needs_context: Nothing to approve: the context has not been uploaded, or must be uploaded again
build_queued_hint: The concurrent build limit ([registry] max_concurrent_builds) has been reached. The task starts automatically after a running build completes.
no_builds_hint: Submit an image build task using the build form.
no_images_hint: The whitelist is empty — a platform admin must add one (CLI for now).
submissions_subtitle: Review queue for user-uploaded modpacks. Approved submissions will automatically trigger safe Kaniko builds with Trivy scans.
reject_dialog_desc: Please provide a detailed reason for rejecting this modpack submission. This reason will be shown to the user.
no_submissions_hint: There are currently no pending or reviewed modpack submissions.
updates_subtitle: Host status, backups, the off-site copy, diagnostics, and versions.
updates_window_advisory: Apply is allowed inside this window. The host checks it before taking a backup and again before installation. Outside the window, apply is refused unless `--now` explicitly starts manual maintenance; `--force` does not bypass the checks.
updates_current_unset: No maintenance window set. Configure one before applying, or explicitly use `--apply --now` for manual maintenance.
updates_validation_both: Both start and end times must be set, or both cleared.
updates_validation_order: End time must be strictly after start time.
updates_timezone_hint: Times are selected and displayed in your browser's local time zone ({{tz}}).
dbbackup_subtitle: The control-plane database stores users, Passkeys, server ownership, quotas, audit logs, and world archive indexes. It is backed up daily, and a separate snapshot is created before upgrade migrations.
dbbackup_stale_title: The newest backup is more than {{hours}} hours old
dbbackup_daily_stale_title: The daily backup last completed {{when}}, past the {{hours}}-hour limit
dbbackup_daily_never_title: The daily timer has not completed a backup
dbbackup_daily_fix_hint: The newer backup was created manually or by another task and is available for restoration. It does not confirm that the daily timer is healthy; check the timer on the Diagnostics tab.
dbbackup_servers_title: The newest backup lacks the server definitions
dbbackup_servers_hint: The cluster did not respond during backup, so server definitions are missing. Restoring the database alone cannot recreate servers. Back up again after cluster connectivity recovers.
dbbackup_fix_hint: Without a valid database backup, host failure may prevent recovery of accounts, server ownership, and archive indexes. Back up now, and check the daily timer on the Diagnostics tab.
dbbackup_offsite_note: Backups are stored only on this host. Disk or host failure may affect both backups and original data. Configure an independent bucket on the Off-site copy tab.
versions_subtitle: felis-update-check.timer compares installed component versions with upstream releases daily. Felis does not apply updates automatically.
versions_apply_hint: Run this read-only check on the host. It shows the target, scope and an exact `--apply` command. Review it, then run that command during the maintenance window:
versions_stale_title: The newest version check is more than {{hours}} hours old
versions_fix_hint: The displayed version information may be outdated. Run a new check on the host and inspect the timer logs to determine why the scheduled check did not run:
build_import_submission_more: Displaying the latest {{shown}} of {{total}} submissions. Use search to locate older submissions.
build_import_search_placeholder: Search submissions by name, ID or submitter
build_import_submission_hint: Selecting a submission automatically populates the Image Reference, Context Reference, and the corresponding Dockerfile audit header.
build_import_submission_warning_desc: Manually triggering a build will not automatically mark this submission as approved, nor will it update its associated build status in the database. Use for emergency debugging or testing only.
users_subtitle: Manage platform user accounts, quotas, and sessions.
users_create_desc: Create a new platform account. Accounts are passwordless — the user signs in with an in-game /link bind code, or with email verification / a passkey once bound.
user_not_found_body: The account does not exist or has been deleted. Return to the user list and search again.
users_empty_hint: No users match the current filters.
users_role_locked_self: The current account’s role cannot be changed.
users_role_locked_owner: The Owner role cannot be changed. Manage it through the host recovery console (sudo felis breakGlass).
users_unlink_dlg_desc: Are you sure you want to unlink this Minecraft account? The user will lose any in-game identity tied to this UUID.
users_session_revoke_one_dlg_desc: Are you sure you want to revoke this session? The user will be logged out from this device immediately.
users_session_revoke_all_dlg_desc: Are you sure you want to revoke all active sessions? The user will be logged out from every device.
users_protected_self: The signed-in account cannot be disabled or deleted.
users_protected_owner: The Owner account cannot be disabled or deleted from the panel. Manage it through the host recovery console (sudo felis breakGlass).
users_danger_disable_desc: Prevent this user from logging in. All active sessions will be revoked immediately.
users_danger_enable_desc: Allow this user to log in again.
users_danger_disable_dlg_desc: This user will be unable to log in. All active sessions will be revoked immediately.
users_danger_enable_dlg_desc: This user will be able to log in again.
users_danger_delete_dlg_desc: This action is permanent. The user's owned servers will be released, all sessions revoked, and the account permanently disabled. This cannot be undone through the panel.
users_danger_delete_desc: Soft-delete this user. Owned servers are released, all sessions are revoked, and the account is permanently disabled. This action cannot be undone through the panel.
users_danger_passkeys_desc: Remove all Passkeys registered to this account to address lost or compromised authenticators. Other sign-in methods, including email codes and in-game approval, remain available.
users_danger_passkeys_dlg_desc: All Passkeys registered to this account will be permanently removed. Other sign-in methods remain available. Keys can be registered again from Account after sign-in.
add_image_desc: Register an external Docker image reference on the whitelist for later server creation.
search_no_results_hint: Try a different search term or filter.
trigger_build_desc: Enter the build parameters to launch a Kaniko pipeline job in an isolated namespace.
builds_search_placeholder: Search build ID, image reference, or status...
builds_refresh_failed: Unable to refresh the build list: {{reason}}
scan_none: This build has no retained security scan record. It may have ended before scanning or been created before scan retention was enabled.
scan_load_failed: Unable to load the security scan: {{reason}}
scan_policy: Blocks on {{severities}}; vulnerabilities with no fixed release are listed only
scan_policy_unfixed: Blocks on {{severities}}, including vulnerabilities with no fixed release
scan_clean: Trivy detected no findings in this image.
scan_showing: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} findings. The full report lists every one.
scan_policy_accepts_one: {{count}} ID accepted as a known risk
scan_accepted_title: Listed in [registry] scan_accept as a known risk, so it never blocks.
scan_not_kept: The file was not retained for this build. It may have exceeded the size limit or its generation step may have failed.
mail_description: Sign-in codes, identity confirmations and alerts are sent through this relay. Settings saved here override those written by felis setup at install time and apply at once to the API, the watchdog, idle cleanup and break-glass sign-in, without a restart.
mail_from_hint: It must be a sending identity your mail provider has authorized; otherwise the provider rejects mail at delivery.
mail_password_kept: Saved; leave empty to keep it
mail_cap_hint: 0 uses the default cap of 120 messages per hour. Keep it at or below your mail provider's limit.
mail_tls_hint: When on, mail is refused if the server does not offer STARTTLS. Turn it off only for a server reached over a trusted internal network.
mail_test_sent: A test message was sent to {{to}}.
mail_saved: Mail delivery is saved and in effect.
mail_clear_confirm: Felis will use the relay felis setup wrote at install time. If none was configured then, sign-in codes cannot be mailed.
mail_save_hint: Saving first sends one self-test message to the sender address, and saves only once it is delivered.
platform_subtitle: Manage player entry, notifications and retention, access and security, and distributed nodes.
platform_limit_hint: 0 means unlimited. New starts count servers already running or requested to run; system services can always start. Lowering the limit does not stop existing servers.
platform_cooldown_hint: Minimum interval between accepted wake requests for the same server. 0 disables the cooldown.
platform_scope: The limit applies to panel starts, in-game wakes and scheduled starts. It is an admission check; available memory still determines whether Kubernetes can schedule a server. User quotas remain under Users.
platform_saved: Saved. The new policy is active without a restart.
platform_live: Saved changes apply immediately on all API replicas.
platform_distribution_architecture: Controllers run the API, operator, database, registry, and public entry point. Workers run game servers and maintenance tasks. With controller high availability, the control plane moves between several controllers; when a worker is lost, its servers can be moved to other nodes from their backups, manually or automatically.
platform_distribution_enable_hint: Enabling distributed mode requires installer configuration of controller identity, WireGuard, archive transport, and node isolation during a maintenance window. This deployment configuration cannot be switched live from the panel.
platform_distribution_prepare: Back up the database and k3s state, configure the controller using the deployment runbook, and update the complete peer address list on all existing nodes. Workers must use the same architecture and k3s version as the controller.
platform_distribution_token: On the controller, create a separate expiring bootstrap token for each worker as root. Transfer the token file over trusted SSH/SCP. Do not provide the server token or administrator kubeconfig to workers. Replace command placeholders with actual values.
platform_distribution_worker: Run felis node join on the worker using the runbook, supplying the controller address, fixed node address, token file, Registry address, and complete peer list. New nodes remain isolated with NoSchedule until approval.
platform_distribution_approve: Approve the node from the controller. The command verifies identity, network isolation, image pulling, and cross-node connectivity. Failed checks preserve isolation. Approval removes the specified cached image and must run before the node hosts game workloads.
platform_distribution_management: Online approved workers can be selected when creating a server. Existing servers must be fully stopped before migration. Successful migration leaves the server stopped and retains its source world volume.
node_control_description: Enable distributed deployment, enroll workers, run admission checks, enable controller high availability and add controllers. Tasks execute on the controller host; panel disconnection does not terminate a task.
node_control_unavailable: Host node service is not installed. Update the controller installation to enable panel management.
node_control_confirm_enable_ha: Database and cluster backups are authorized, together with moving k3s to embedded etcd, installing Longhorn, and moving the database, uploads, registry, archive, and the Login and Lobby worlds onto replicated volumes. Login and Lobby pause during the move and the panel is briefly unavailable; other game servers keep running.
node_control_confirm_join_controller: Adding this host as a controller is authorized: every node's firewall is updated, the cluster tokens, the Felis configuration (including database credentials) and the felis binary are transferred over SSH, and the k3s server and Felis host services are installed. Game servers keep running.
node_control_controller_ip_hint: Required. Enter the fixed IP configured on the new controller.
node_control_ha_hint: Controller high availability keeps the cluster state in embedded etcd and the control-plane data on three-replica Longhorn volumes. etcd requires a majority of controllers online, so deploy three or more controllers, an odd number, to tolerate the loss of one; controllers should share one low-latency network. A new controller requires the same architecture as the existing ones and a host without k3s.
node_control_stage_install_ha: Enable embedded etcd and replicated storage
node_control_confirm_upgrade: Game and maintenance workloads on the target node are stopped. Moving the node's felis binary and k3s to the controller's versions and reinstalling its peer firewall is authorized; k3s-agent restarts.
node_control_ssh_hint: Use an alias from the controller root SSH configuration or user@host. Noninteractive authentication and verified host fingerprints are required.
node_control_peers_hint: Enter exact /32 or /128 addresses separated by commas. Existing nodes and the new node are included automatically.
node_control_confirm_enable: All game servers (including Login and Lobby) and maintenance tasks are stopped. Database and cluster backups and controller network changes are authorized. Panel access may be temporarily interrupted.
node_control_confirm_worker: Game and maintenance workloads on the target node are stopped. Node installation, peer firewall updates, image pulls and network isolation checks are authorized.
node_control_prerequisites_body: Controller and workers require matching architecture and k3s versions and fixed addresses. SSH accounts require root or sudo -n access. Configure keys and verify host fingerprints on the controller host before first use; unknown fingerprints are rejected. Existing worker SSH aliases must match node names for peer firewall updates. Enrollment requires a host without k3s. Nodes already joined after an interrupted enrollment must use “Approve existing worker”. Failed admission retains quarantine and does not start game servers.
node_control_connection_lost: Task status is temporarily unavailable: {{error}}. Polling resumes when connectivity is restored; the last confirmed status remains visible.
node_control_retry_hint: Verify current host state and resolve the failure before retrying. Retry creates a new task and repeats checks. Already enrolled workers require approval instead of enrollment.
node_control_other_running: Another node task is running; new node operations are temporarily blocked.
node_control_enable_required: The platform is in single-node mode. Enable distributed deployment before enrolling or approving workers. Activation changes controller configuration and may temporarily interrupt panel access.
node_control_enable_ip_hint: Required. Enter the controller’s currently registered fixed IP, using a static address or DHCP reservation.
node_control_ip_hint: Required. Enter the fixed IP configured on the target worker.
node_control_incomplete: Complete all required fields and acknowledge the maintenance conditions before executing.
entry_description: Configure game identity verification, panel account linking and destination independently. Existing deployments retain their current flow until the first save.
entry_lobby_hint: Authenticate, then enter the lobby to choose a server.
entry_direct_hint: Authenticate, then enter the selected main server.
entry_domain_hint: Select the destination using the connection hostname.
entry_main_hint: All entry hostnames lead to this server. Its autostart policy still controls startup permission.
entry_default_hint: Used for unmatched hostnames. Without a default, web sign-in connections enter the lobby; other connections are rejected.
entry_wake_hint: The waiting space must be running. Startup failure or timeout is reported; a connection waiting in Limbo is then disconnected.
entry_web_wait: Web sign-in uses the lobby while waiting for startup.
entry_link_hint: Players must complete web sign-in in Limbo when enabled. Otherwise game identity is still verified and panel linking remains optional.
entry_components: Web sign-in requires the login space and lobby. Automatic authentication only requires the selected destination and waiting space. Unused spaces can be stopped manually.
entry_scope: Applies to new connections within 15 seconds. Current players are unaffected.
entry_saved: Entry policy saved. New connections use it after the proxy refreshes its configuration.
failover_description: When a node is lost, its worlds can be brought back on other nodes from each server's newest intact backup. This applies to workers and, with controller high availability, to controllers. By default the Owner confirms it under Execution nodes, after seeing how much progress it loses.
failover_auto_hint: When exactly one node is lost and a controller is up, its worlds move to the least loaded online node once it has been lost for the set time. When several nodes are lost at once, the Owner decides.
failover_after: Minutes lost before an automatic failover
failover_after_hint: 10 to 1440 minutes. A shorter wait fails over sooner, and a brief network outage is more likely to set it off.
failover_replica_hint: Servers running on a worker (and, with controller high availability, on a controller) are copied live this often, so a failover loses at most that much progress. 0 turns the copies off; otherwise 15 to 1440 minutes. Each server keeps only its newest 2 replicas.
failover_invalid: The automatic failover waits 10 to 1440 minutes, and the replica interval is 0 or 15 to 1440 minutes.
retention_description: How many backups of each server are kept and for how long, how often the scheduled restore points come, the backup store's cap, and how long audit rows are kept. These settings take precedence over felis.toml; felis-api applies them at once, and the backup and reaper jobs on their next run.
retention_manualKeep_hint: 1 to 100. The oldest is removed beyond it.
retention_manualCooldownMinutes_hint: 0 to 1440. 0 sets no limit; administrators are not held to it.
retention_scheduledEveryHours_hint: 0 to 720. Only worlds played since their last point get one; 0 turns them off.
retention_releasedRetentionDays: Days a removed world's archive is kept
retention_releasedRetentionDays_hint: 1 to 3650 days. A world reclaimed for idleness, released or deleted is archived first; that archive is kept this long.
retention_maxStoreGiB_hint: 0 sets no cap. At the cap, manual backups and scheduled points pause.
retention_auditRetentionDays_hint: 0 keeps every row; otherwise 30 to 3650 days.
retention_clear_confirm: felis.toml's [archive] and [audit] settings apply again, and the values saved here are discarded.
heartbeat_description: With the heartbeat URL of an external monitoring service (for example Healthchecks.io), every run of the Felis watchdog pings it; when the pings stop, for example because the host is down or the watchdog itself failed, the service alerts you. A URL set here takes precedence over the one the installer wrote on the host.
heartbeat_replace: Replace with a new heartbeat URL
heartbeat_url_hint: A full address starting with http:// or https://. Its path is the check's key, so only the scheme and host are shown once saved.
heartbeat_saved: Heartbeat URL saved. The watchdog uses it on its next run.
heartbeat_cleared: The panel's heartbeat URL is removed; if the installer wrote one on the host, the watchdog uses that one.
heartbeat_clear_confirm: Once removed, the watchdog stops pinging this URL and the monitoring service alerts on the missing pings. Pause the check at the service as well.
heartbeat_footer: The watchdog runs every two minutes.
default_language_description: Sets the interface language for new visitors and for users who have not chosen a language in the panel. A language chosen in the panel takes precedence. Notification emails remain bilingual.
default_language_hint: With Follow browser language, the panel uses the language of the visitor's browser and shows English when that language is not supported.
default_language_live: Applies the next time the panel loads.
host_task_other_running: Another host task is running. This action becomes available when it finishes.
host_cloudflare_login: Authorize this host in your Cloudflare account. The task continues automatically after authorization.
host_stage_stop_control_plane: Stopping the panel and the operator
host_stage_start_control_plane: Starting the panel and the operator
host_alerts_unreadable: The alert state could not be read: {{error}}
host_quiet_hint: A hold suppresses watchdog email during planned maintenance. Checks continue, and alerts remain listed here.
host_proxy_ok: The game proxy at {{address}} accepts connections.
host_proxy_down: The game proxy at {{address}} refuses connections.
dbbackup_offsite_on: Backups are also copied hourly, encrypted, to the bucket configured on the Off-site copy tab.
db_bundles_description: Each backup can be verified or restored. A restore stops the panel and the operator while it runs, and the current database is backed up first. All users sign in again afterwards.
db_bundles_none: No database backups on this host
db_bundle_newest: The newest backup is the latest restore point and cannot be deleted
db_delete_description: {{name}} is deleted from this host. A copy with the same name in the off-site copy is not affected. This cannot be undone.
db_schedule_hint: The time follows the host's clock. Saving rewrites the timer and takes one backup immediately.
db_schedule_custom: The timer uses a custom calendar expression. Saving a time replaces it.
db_restore_description: Every table is replaced with the contents of this backup. The panel and the operator stop during the restore; the current database is backed up first, and all users must sign in again afterwards.
db_restore_type: Enter the backup name to confirm: {{name}}
world_backup_description: Archives the worlds of user servers one at a time. Running servers are backed up live: saving pauses while the world is copied, and players stay connected.
world_backup_stop_hint: Players are disconnected, and the servers remain stopped after the backup. Servers that are starting or stopping are included only with this option.
world_backup_stop_confirm: Running servers are stopped before their worlds are archived. Their players are disconnected, and the servers stay stopped afterwards.
offsite_description: Every hour the host encrypts world archives, database backups, user images, and submission uploads, and copies them to an S3-compatible bucket. The copies can be read only with this host's encryption key.
offsite_key_mismatch: The bucket's objects are sealed with a different key than this host's. Nothing is copied until the keys match.
offsite_standby: Host {{host}} writes this bucket. This host stands by and does not copy.
offsite_displaced: Host {{host}} has taken this bucket over. This host no longer copies.
offsite_not_configured: No off-site bucket is configured. Every backup is stored only on this host.
offsite_prefix_hint: Lets several installations share one bucket.
offsite_keys_keep: Leave both keys empty to keep the current credentials.
offsite_db_keep: Database backups kept in the bucket
offsite_seal_key_hint: Leave empty to generate a new key. Enter the existing key when the bucket already holds copies from a previous host.
offsite_key_hint: Without this key the copies in the bucket cannot be read. Keep it somewhere other than this host.
offsite_saved_reload: The configuration is saved. Reload to see the new status.
offsite_disable_confirm: The hourly copy stops, and new backups stay on this host only. Copies already in the bucket and the encryption key are kept.
offsite_take_over_confirm: This host becomes the one that writes the bucket, and the host that wrote it before stops copying. Use this only when this host permanently replaces that one.
restore_host_description: Restores the database, user images, uploads, servers, and worlds from the off-site bucket. It is intended for a newly installed host that replaces a lost one. The panel is unavailable while the database is restored, and users sign in again afterwards.
restore_host_needs_offsite: Configure the off-site bucket on this host first, with the encryption key of the host being replaced.
restore_host_bundle_hint: Leave empty to use the newest backup. List bucket contents on the Off-site copy card shows the available backups.
restore_host_take_over_hint: Turn this off when this host is a rehearsal and the original host keeps running.
restore_host_force_hint: Required when this installation already holds servers. Their data is replaced.
restore_host_confirm: The database of this installation is replaced by the off-site copy, and servers and worlds are restored from it. The panel stops while the database is restored.
doctor_description: Runs every check the watchdog runs, plus the host's services, timers, and alert delivery, and shows where to look next. No email is sent.
support_description: Collects status, health checks, logs, and cluster state into one redacted archive to attach when asking for help. Credentials are removed from it.
support_server_logs_hint: Game logs contain player names, IP addresses, and chat. Include them only when the issue concerns a server.
audit_export_description: Downloads audit records as JSON lines, so they can be kept beyond the audit retention period, after which they are deleted.
audit_export_bounds: Leave a date empty to export from the oldest or to the newest record.
audit_export_order: The end date must be after the start date.
access_description: Choose how the panel is reached. Changing the method restarts the panel; with Cloudflare, the admin console is protected by Cloudflare Access.
access_mode_local_hint: The panel is reached at the host's address and port. Switching to this method removes a Cloudflare tunnel and reopens the panel port.
access_mode_reverse-proxy_hint: A reverse proxy such as Caddy, nginx, or Traefik terminates TLS in front of the panel and passes the visitor address in X-Forwarded-For.
access_mode_cloudflare_hint: The host creates a tunnel, routes the hostnames, and puts Cloudflare Access in front of the admin console. The panel port is then closed to the public.
access_identity_hint: An email address, or @ followed by an email domain.
access_token_hint: It needs permission to edit Access applications and DNS. It is used for this change only and is not stored.
access_confirm: The panel restarts and may become reachable at a different address. Passkeys are bound to the panel hostname; changing it requires registering them again.
domain_hint: Moves the installation to a new root domain on every surface that carries it. DNS records must already point to this host.
domain_confirm: The installation moves to {{domain}}. All users must sign in again, and Passkeys registered for the old panel hostname stop working.
storage_description: Where build contexts uploaded with submissions are kept. Changing it restarts the panel; existing uploads are not moved.
storage_keys_hint: The bucket is checked before anything changes. The keys are kept on the host and must be entered again to change.
storage_confirm: The panel restarts briefly. Uploads already stored remain in their current location.
credentials_description: Replaces a generated credential and restarts what uses it. Rotate after a suspected leak, or when staff with host access leave.
credential_velocity_impact: The panel restarts briefly. The proxy loads the new token without disconnecting players, or restarts if it has not loaded it within a minute.
credential_limbo_impact: The panel and the login space restart; players in the login space are disconnected.
credential_build_impact: The panel restarts briefly; running builds may fail and must be started again.
credential_registry_impact: The registry and the panel restart; image pulls and builds pause briefly.
credential_forwarding_impact: The proxy and every running game server restart; all players are disconnected.
credential_db_impact: The database password and every configuration that carries it change, and the panel restarts.
proxy_description: Memory ceiling of the Velocity proxy. The default 1G suits about 100 concurrent players.
proxy_heap_hint: 256M to 64G, for example 768M or 2G. The value is kept across installer reruns and updates.
proxy_confirm: The proxy restarts with the new memory ceiling, and all players are disconnected.
converge_description: Creates the login space and the lobby again when either is missing, and adds settings that newer releases introduced to servers created earlier: new fields on the login space and the lobby, and idle auto-stop on older user servers.
converge_rcon: Enable RCON on older user servers
converge_rcon_hint: Live backups and console commands require RCON. A server whose image has no RCON listener may then fail to start; enable this only for images that support it.
node_control_vip_hint: An unused IPv4 address that follows the active controller, so players and the panel keep one address after a failover. The installer chooses the interface and router ID when they are left empty.
self_service_description: When on, users without a quota of their own can create servers within the default quota below, and their claims and resource changes are held to it as well. Users with their own quota keep it.
self_service_enabled_hint: When off, users without their own quota cannot create servers, and their claims are not limited.
self_service_caps_hint: Leave a field empty for no limit; enter 0 to grant none of that resource.
self_service_invalid: Enter non-negative numbers; the server count must be a whole number.
self_service_saved: The default quota has been saved.
user_quota_default_on: This user is held to the default quota: {{caps}}.
user_quota_default_off: Self-service servers are off: this user cannot create servers, and claims and resource changes are not limited.
user_quota_default_where: The default quota is changed under "Self-service servers and default quota" on the user list.
user_quota_custom_hint: An own quota takes precedence over the default quota. Leave a field empty for no limit; enter 0 to grant none of it. A lower quota limits later creation, claims and resizes, and leaves existing servers as they are.
user_quota_cleared: This user is now held to the default quota.
